caveats:
This rapid and experimental damage proxy product has not been triangulated, validated or confirmed building damage assessment. It features considerable backscatter intensities anomalies likely to be caused by earthquake-related damage. 

Backscatter intensities anomalies can be influenced by structural damage, building density, rubble and debris, surface moisture, vegetation, topography, sensor geometry, radar shadow and scene footprints intersections. The product therefore cannot determine whether an individual building structure is damaged, destroyed, safe or suitable for return.

Buildings not screened as likely damaged may be smaller in surface, outside meaningful analysis area, missing from the baseline building dataset, or unaffected. They must not be interpreted as undamaged or unassessed. 

Users should triangulate results with field assessments, VHR satellite imagery, local and national authorities, and similar assessment products.

bdg_sfc is the total surface of the original likely damaged Overture building footprints, while b_aff_sf is the affected building surface intersecting at least 50% of the Sentinel-1 SAR damage proxy (both in square meters).
methodology_other:
Our experimental SAR analysis is utilizing the z-score anomaly of Sentinel-1 GRD backscatter amplitudes between a pre-event annual baseline and two post-event matched acquisitions on 25.06.2026. 

This SAR product estimates 81,437 likely damaged buildings across the analyzed impacted area. A building footprint is included where at least 50% of its footprint surface overlaps a built-up-masked Sentinel-1 damage proxy using the GHSL-BUILT-S product.

This preliminary damage proxy product is intended to support rapid screening and prioritization, targeting of follow-up assessment, triangulation with VHR optical and radar images, and other damage assessments and products.
name: venezuela-earthquakes-damage-assessment-using-sentinel-1-radar-data
notes:
This dataset provides a rapid experimental Sentinel-1-based damage assessment product for the broader impacted area from the 24 June 2026 Venezuelan earthquakes. It includes both the entire analyzed area of the SAR analysis and the Overture Maps building footprints identified as likely damaged. 

This SAR product estimates 81,437 likely damaged buildings across the analyzed impacted area.

This preliminary damage proxy product is intended to support rapid screening and prioritization, targeting of follow-up assessment, triangulation with VHR optical and radar images, and other damage assessments and products.
